summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to provide NAT egress for node2 and node3 on a private /24 (10.60.60.0/24 over eth1), implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the pre-provisioned control node). node1 got a static LAN address (10.60.60.254/24 on eth1) plus a VyOS source-NAT masquerade rule (10.60.60.0/24 -> eth0). node2/node3 got a new NetworkManager eth1 profile (10.60.60.11/.12) with a lower-metric default route via node1, so their default internet path now genuinely transits node1's NAT. Verified via api.ipify.org and live NAT translation tables. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node2, node3, node1, node4), confirming a changed boot_id and full recovery of NAT config, network profiles, and Ansible tooling after each restart, plus a clean idempotent playbook re-run at the end.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router (eth0 mgmt/WAN with internet, eth1 unconfigured private LAN), node2/node3=RHEL7.9 (eth0 mgmt, eth1 unconfigured private LAN), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 pre-provisioned Ansible control node with ansible-core 2.20 and SSH key material

Established SSH access from node4 to targets: added node4's pubkey to VyOS node1 via 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' (VyOS hardcodes PermitRootLogin no, so root SSH is impossible), and to antrieb's authorized_keys on node2/node3
Captured pre-change baseline: eth1 had no IP on any node; node2 showed 100% ping loss to 8.8.8.8 over eth1

Playbook play 1 (host group 'router'/node1): bash+VyOS script-template shell task to set eth1 address 10.60.60.254/24 and NAT source masquerade rule 100 (source 10.60.60.0/24, out-interface eth0), then commit+save

Playbook play 2 (host group 'lan_hosts'/node2,node3): used ansible.builtin.raw (RHEL7 only has Python 2.7, incompatible with modern Ansible module code) to idempotently create an nmcli eth1 connection profile with static IP, gateway 10.60.60.254, and route-metric 50 (lower than the existing eth0 default route's metric 100), then bring it up and verify with a ping test

Ran the playbook successfully; independently verified via exec: node2/node3 ip route shows eth1 default route preferred, curl to api.ipify.org returns node1's WAN IP (198.58.243.18), and node1's 'show nat source translations' shows live masqueraded sessions from both LAN hosts

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol sequentially on node2, node3, node1, then node4: captured boot_id + health baseline, issued native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified full recovery of NAT/routing/connectivity (and, for node4, a clean idempotent playbook re-run) before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: node1 provides NAT so node2/node3 can reach the internet through it
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run shows node1's NAT rule/eth1 configured and node2/node3 pinging 8.8.8.8 successfully over eth1; independent exec verification shows both nodes' default route now goes via node1 (metric 50 < eth0's 100), curl to api.ipify.org returns node1's WAN IP 198.58.243.18, and node1's live NAT translation table shows active masqueraded sessions from 10.60.60.11 and 10.60.60.12 to 10.100.76.10

Playbook syntax-checked and executed from node4 (control node) against inventory covering node1 (VyOS) and node2/node3 (RHEL7); final idempotent re-run after all restarts shows ok/changed=0-1 with no failures

evidence.requirement: Pre-change baseline: private network had no internet access of its own
evidence.summary: Before configuration, node2 showed 100% packet loss pinging 8.8.8.8 sourced from eth1 (private network, unaddressed, no NAT)

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: boot identity change + service/data recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 738d0aac captured with healthy NAT-routed egress; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); post-reboot boot_id 0ca9c5da (changed); recovered state shows eth1/eth0 connections active, correct routes, and successful internet egress via node1's NAT

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: boot identity change + service/data recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 325732f1 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 8e46513a (changed); recovered state shows eth1/eth0 active, correct routes, successful egress via node1's NAT

evidence.requirement: node1 (router) restart: boot identity change + NAT/service recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4098161f captured with NAT rule and eth1 config confirmed; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id 9ddb11b5 (changed), confirmed via both direct exec and independent SSH poll from node4; recovered state shows NAT rule, eth1 address, and ip_forward=1 all restored from saved VyOS config, and node2/node3 continued reaching the internet through it

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart: boot identity change + tooling/data recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 416c5cf5 captured with ansible project files present; reboot issued (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id 5f1ed85e (changed); recovered state confirmed by playbook syntax-check passing and a full idempotent playbook re-run succeeding against all managed nodes
